title: Ensure SSH Protocol Version 2 is Configured
description: Legacy SSH version 1 contains fundamental cryptographic flaws and must be disabled. Only SSH version 2 should be permitted for remote network administration.
rationale: SSHv1 is susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks and insertion attacks. SSHv2 provides strong confidentiality, integrity, and replay protection.

title: Ensure Insecure Telnet Protocol is Disabled
description: Telnet transmits authentication credentials and configuration commands in plaintext across the network, exposing credentials to packet sniffing.
rationale: Cleartext management protocols expose administrative credentials to packet sniffing on local and transit network segments.

title: Ensure Insecure HTTP Server is Disabled
description: HTTP web management does not encrypt web traffic, exposing session tokens and administrative actions to interception.
rationale: Cleartext HTTP exposes device web administrative sessions to eavesdropping and credential theft.

title: Ensure Secure HTTPS Server is Enabled (if web management required)
description: Where web management is utilized, HTTPS with TLS encryption must be enabled to ensure transport confidentiality.
rationale: HTTPS ensures administrative web sessions are encrypted using TLS.

title: Ensure Password Minimum Length is at Least 14 Characters
description: Short passwords are vulnerable to dictionary and brute-force cracking attacks. Administrative accounts must enforce a minimum length of 14 characters.
rationale: Passwords of 14 or more characters offer significant resistance against offline brute-force cracking.

title: Ensure Administrative Session Timeout is Configured <= 600 Seconds
description: Unattended administrative sessions must automatically terminate after an inactivity period not exceeding 10 minutes (600 seconds).
rationale: Terminating idle management sessions mitigates unauthorized access from abandoned administrative terminals.

title: Ensure Legal Warning Login Banner is Configured
description: A legal advisory banner must be presented prior to authentication warning that access is restricted to authorized personnel and activities are monitored.
rationale: Warning banners establish legal basis for prosecuting unauthorized system intruders.

title: Ensure Centralized Syslog Logging is Enabled
description: Audit and security logs must be forwarded to a dedicated remote syslog or SIEM server for incident analysis and non-repudiation.
rationale: Centralized logging prevents an intruder from tampering with local device logs to conceal illicit activities.

title: Ensure Network Time Protocol (NTP) Synchronization is Configured
description: Accurate timestamps are critical for correlating security events across distributed systems during digital forensics.
rationale: Synchronized time guarantees forensic validity and accurate chronology in security audits.

title: Ensure SNMP Enforces Version 3 Only and Default Communities are Removed
description: SNMPv1 and SNMPv2c transmit community strings in cleartext and lack cryptographic integrity. SNMPv3 with auth and priv must be enforced.
rationale: Default SNMP communities (public/private) allow unauthorized device enumeration and configuration modification.

title: Ensure AAA Authentication Login is Enforced
description: Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) provides centralized identity management and granular privilege control.
rationale: Centralized AAA enforces organizational identity policies and prevents shared credential abuse.

title: Ensure Insecure FTP Server Daemon is Disabled
description: FTP transmits administrative credentials and firmware data in unencrypted plaintext, vulnerable to passive interception.
rationale: Cleartext file transfers allow interception of firmware images and sensitive configuration artifacts.

title: Ensure Auxiliary (AUX) Console Port is Disabled
description: Auxiliary ports can be exploited via modem connections or unmonitored serial cables to bypass standard network access controls.
rationale: Unused auxiliary ports represent an uncontrolled physical backdoor into device management.

title: Ensure Local Password Hash Encryption Service is Enabled
description: All passwords stored in local configuration files must be cryptographically hashed or obscured to prevent shoulder surfing.
rationale: Plaintext passwords in configuration backups allow rapid compromise by unauthorized staff.

title: Ensure Login Failure Rate Limiting or Lockout is Configured
description: Network devices must enforce quiet periods or login delays following repeated unsuccessful authentication attempts.
rationale: Mitigates automated brute-force attacks against administrative credentials.

title: Ensure IP Source Routing is Disabled
description: IP source routing permits packet senders to specify network transit paths, bypassing firewall state inspection and boundary routing.
rationale: Adversaries can exploit source routing to bypass boundary firewalls and perimeter access controls.

title: Ensure ICMP Redirects are Disabled
description: ICMP redirects can be injected by malicious local devices to hijack and reroute legitimate network traffic flows.
rationale: Prevents malicious manipulation of host and router route caches via rogue ICMP packets.

title: Ensure IP Directed Broadcasts are Disabled
description: Directed broadcast packets allow remote attackers to amplify denial-of-service attacks against subnets (e.g. Smurf attacks).
rationale: Directed broadcasts can be weaponized in amplification and distributed denial-of-service floods.

title: Ensure Proxy ARP is Disabled Across Interfaces
description: Proxy ARP causes routers to respond to ARP requests on behalf of other hosts, obscuring routing issues and increasing MITM risks.
rationale: Disabling Proxy ARP prevents topology leakage and reduces ARP spoofing exposure.

title: Ensure Unicast Reverse Path Forwarding (uRPF) is Enabled
description: uRPF ensures the router only forwards packets whose source IP address matches the FIB routing table for the incoming interface.
rationale: Blocks spoofed source IP addresses commonly utilized in reflection and DDoS attacks.

title: Ensure Detailed Timestamps are Enabled for System Logging
description: Log timestamps must include millisecond precision and explicit timezone or UTC indicators for accurate forensic correlation.
rationale: Imprecise timestamps make multi-device incident reconstruction ambiguous and legally unviable.

title: Ensure Internal Log Buffer Size and Severity is Configured
description: An internal memory buffer must store recent audit messages in the event remote syslog servers are temporarily unreachable.
rationale: Preserves critical failure messages locally during network disruptions.

title: Ensure NTP Authentication is Configured with Trusted Keys
description: NTP associations must be cryptographically authenticated to prevent spoofed time-shifting attacks.
rationale: Rogue NTP servers can invalidate cryptographic certificates and compromise audit timelines.

title: Ensure SNMPv3 Privacy (AES Encryption) is Enforced
description: SNMPv3 sessions must use authPriv security level with AES encryption to prevent payload sniffing of OID telemetry.
rationale: Unencrypted SNMP polling can reveal internal IP topologies and system parameters.

title: Ensure Control Plane Policing (CoPP) is Enabled
description: Control plane policing limits traffic arriving at the route processor CPU, protecting against control-plane exhaustion DoS.
rationale: Prevents processor exhaustion and routing protocol flapping caused by malicious traffic floods.

title: Ensure BGP Neighbor Authentication is Configured
description: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) peer sessions must use TCP MD5 or keychain authentication to prevent route hijacking.
rationale: Prevents unauthorized peers from injecting forged routes or resetting active peering sessions.
